steps.title: Prepare yeast paste
steps.instruction: Mix approximately 10 g of instant dried yeast with 12 mL of water in a 100 mL beaker until a thick, creamy consistency is achieved.

steps.title: Prepare fruit juice agar plates
steps.instruction: Boil 9 g agar in 300 mL distilled water; separately dissolve 10 g sucrose in 100 mL apple or cranberry juice. Combine the two solutions, pour into 50 mm‑diameter, 20.3 mm‑high Petri dishes to a depth of ~15 mm, let cool and dry at room temperature for ~1 h (plates can be stored at 4 °C for 2–3 days). Immediately before use, add a button‑sized drop of the yeast paste to each plate and let dry.

steps.title: Prepare heptane glue
steps.instruction: Fill a 50 mL conical tube with ~1 m of double‑sided sticky tape (tightly packed), add 20 mL heptane, and rotate overnight. Remove the tape, centrifuge the heptane at 15 700 RCF to pellet solids, and keep the clarified glue at room temperature in a Parafilm‑sealed Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Set up fly cage and lay eggs
steps.instruction: Place flies in a cage, close the cage with a yeasted fruit‑juice agar plate sealed with tape, invert the cage (plate side down) and incubate at 25 °C. For the next 48 h replace the yeasted plates every 3 h during working hours (≈4 changes per day). On day 3 change the plate, allow flies to lay for 1 h and discard this first collection. Collect embryos from the next plate after an additional 1 h, then age embryos 30 min at 25 °C.

steps.title: Transfer embryos to tape
steps.instruction: Using a paintbrush, transfer embryos from the agar plate onto double‑sided sticky tape affixed to a microscope slide.

steps.title: Crack chorion
steps.instruction: Under a dissecting microscope at 4–7× magnification, gently tap each embryo with a Dumont No. 5 forceps arm to crack the chorion while avoiding damage to the embryo.

steps.title: Remove embryo from chorion
steps.instruction: Touch the end of one forceps arm to the embryo; the embryo will stick to the forceps, leaving the chorion on the tape.

steps.title: Apply heptane glue line
steps.instruction: Dip a 20–200 µL pipette tip into the heptane glue, allow capillary action to fill the tip, and draw a thin line of glue onto the 1.5‑thickness coverslip of a 35 mm glass‑bottom MatTek dish. Let the heptane evaporate, leaving a thin glue layer. Prepare dishes at room temperature and use them the same day.

steps.title: Mount embryos on glue
steps.instruction: Place embryos onto the glued surface, aligning them in a vertical line with ~10–15 embryos per dish (process should take ≤15 min). Ensure embryos desiccate uniformly.

steps.title: Submerge embryos in oil
steps.instruction: Cover the mounted embryos with Voltalef H10S oil (ARKEMA) so they are just submerged, allowing air diffusion while preventing further desiccation.

steps.title: Confocal imaging of embryos
steps.instruction: Place the dish on a spinning‑disc confocal equipped with a 63× 1.4 NA objective and 488 nm (200 µW at sample) and 568 nm (300 µW) lasers. Locate an embryo in cell cycle 10–12, find the brightest centrosome plane, and set a z‑stack that satisfies Nyquist sampling (e.g., 7 images at 0.5 µm intervals, pixel size 0.219 µm). Capture each channel sequentially, minimizing exposure time while avoiding camera saturation. Measure laser power with a Thorlabs slide light meter and adjust software settings so the same laser output at the objective is used for all experiments.

steps.title: Image analysis in FIJI/ImageJ
steps.instruction: Process the acquired images to generate radial fluorescence intensity profiles.

substeps.instruction: Open the image in FIJI/ImageJ.
If two‑channel, split channels (Image > Color > Split Channels).
Scale the image 5‑fold (Image > Scale, bilinear interpolation) to obtain 25 sub‑pixels per original pixel.
Remove pixel scaling (Analyze > Set Scale > Click to remove scale).
Convert to 8‑bit (Image > Type > 8‑bit).
Segment centrosomes using Threshold (Image > Adjust > Threshold, Otsu method) and set levels by eye to obtain a single object per centrosome.
Identify the z‑slice with highest centrosome intensity (best focus).
Draw a circular ROI around a centrosome, sized to enclose it.
Set measurements to include Center of Mass (Analyze > Set Measurements).
Run Analyze > Analyze Particles to obtain the centroid coordinates.
Launch the Radial Profile plugin (Plugins > Radial Profile) and input the centroid coordinates; set the radius to extend beyond the protein signal (same radius for all centrosomes).
Copy the radial values into an Excel spreadsheet.
Subtract the average cytosolic signal (average of the last five radial values).

Normalize intensities: (a) set the peak of each profile to 1 for spatial comparison, or (b) divide by the average peak of wild‑type profiles for abundance comparison (calculate peak with =MAX() and average across centrosomes).
Mirror the profile in Excel to obtain a symmetric centrosomal profile.
Convert pixel units to distance using the known pixel length (5 sub‑pixels = 1 original pixel).
For each condition, compute the average distribution from ≥5 centrosomes in each of ≥7 embryos (minimum 35 measurements).

steps.title: FRAP imaging of centrosomes
steps.instruction: Perform fluorescence recovery after photobleaching on dechorionated embryos.

substeps.instruction: Collect and prepare embryos as described in steps 1–13.
Place the dish on the microscope and set imaging parameters as in the confocal imaging step.
Define a bleaching ROI that slightly exceeds the fluorescent signal of a single centrosome.
Adjust laser settings so the mCherry signal is fully bleached while the GFP marker remains unaffected (e.g., 5 iterations of 100 % 568 nm laser ≈2 mW).
Set post‑bleach acquisition interval according to protein dynamics (e.g., 20 s interval when recovery is measurable within 30 s).
Acquire at least two pre‑bleach frames, bleach the selected centrosomes, then acquire the required post‑bleach time points (collect data from ≥15 centrosomes across ≥5 embryos).
Analyze each time point using the image‑analysis workflow described above.

steps.title: 3D‑SIM imaging of embryos
steps.instruction: Acquire super‑resolution images of centrosomes using structured illumination microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Collect and prepare embryos as in steps 1–13, then place the MatTek dish on the SIM microscope.
Use a 60× 1.42 NA objective with immersion oil of refractive index 1.514 (apply oil to the objective; adjust correction collar to maximize centrosome fluorescence).
Set the z‑stack to a total height of 0.6 µm with 0.125 µm step size.
Choose the shortest camera exposure times that still give sufficient contrast.
Acquire images, recording the red (mCherry) channel first because 488 nm illumination bleaches mCherry.
Determine reconstruction parameters with the SIMcheck plugin, using an empirically derived optical transfer function for the fluorophores and refractive index.
Set the Wiener filter to 0.006 (assess optimal value with SIMcheck).
Reconstruct images using the microscope’s software.

Assess reconstruction quality with SIMcheck: generate modulation contrast‑to‑noise (MCNR) maps (Modulation contrast on raw data). Only use centrosomes located in high‑contrast regions (light‑colored areas).
Discard structures in low‑contrast regions as potential artefacts.
Open raw and reconstructed images in ImageJ and analyze them using the radial‑profile workflow described in step 12.
